title: The magnitude and importance of the project's contribution to the expected scientific, societal and economic impacts
content:
Sub-section 2.3 — The magnitude and importance of the project's contribution to the expected scientific, societal and economic impacts

How the results make a difference beyond the immediate scope. FIELDWISE is a single-researcher action on one development crop, but its contribution is deliberately engineered to reach past that immediate scope along three connected axes — scientific, agricultural/environmental and technological/economic — with a defined European and societal relevance layered on top. The unifying mechanism is that the project does not merely build another crop-stress model; it builds and prospectively tests a validation framework in which operationally obtainable data streams are judged against independent plant-level ground truth and challenged under both unseen-year and genuinely new commercial-field conditions. The result that outlives the action is therefore methodological knowledge: which physiological water-stress relationships survive the transition from proximal measurements toward UAV and Sentinel-2 field-scale monitoring, and which components of the modelling and decision workflow are genuinely reusable beyond the development crop. This is what converts a processing-tomato study into a methodological basis for later crop-by-crop extension across irrigated high-value horticulture — a scientifically controlled pathway rather than an unsupported universalisation from a single crop. Its importance is that it addresses the exact failure mode that limits digital agronomy today: models that fit retrospective data but are never shown to hold under scale change, new seasons and real production settings.

Scientific impact and its magnitude. The scientific contribution is concentrated in three durable, citable objects: the Primary model, benchmark and model card, which reports calibration, uncertainty and blocked unseen-year performance; the Spectral/UAV/Sentinel harmonisation and crop-transfer specification, which enumerates the transferable core components, crop-specific parameters, minimum validation datasets and recalibration gates any later crop must pass; and, above all, the Prospective transferability, uncertainty and limited-recalibration report (due month 18), which quantifies the transfer gap from research experiments to an independent commercial field and states any performance drop honestly rather than hiding it. The magnitude of this contribution is best measured not by a single accuracy figure but by the fact that it delivers a reusable, uncertainty-aware protocol and an openly reported transfer result — a form of high-integrity science that is directly reusable by other groups and that strengthens the research capacity and knowledge transfer of the participating HUN-REN ATK, ELTE and MATE environments through the documented two-way transfer and the planned peer-reviewed publications. This is the project's principal route to the call's expected impact of increased and broadened research and innovation impact (EI-02) and of increased R&I capacity, output and knowledge transfer among European research organisations (EI-05).

Agricultural and environmental impact — credible magnitude with disciplined honesty. FIELDWISE begins with processing tomato precisely because roughly five seasons of heterogeneous scientific observations (2022-2026) already exist, while the intended application domain is irrigated high-value horticulture. Critically, the project makes no fixed-percentage water-saving promise, because real savings depend on crop, cultivar, soil, weather, growth stage, irrigation system and the management action actually taken. What the project provides for magnitude is credible, bounded, literature-referenced context: comparable published studies demonstrate water-saving effects in the approximate 8–30% range under specific strategies — for processing tomato, plant-and-soil monitoring has been reported to reduce irrigation by around 30% versus empirical farmer management and by around 7.5% versus ET-based scheduling in a two-year field trial (Carucci et al. 2023), and early-stage controlled deficit has achieved roughly 25% water saving without statistically significant yield loss while poorly timed deficits reduced yield (Badr et al. 2026). These are stated as bounded context only, never as a FIELDWISE promise; they establish that the magnitude at stake is material and that the water–yield trade-off must be quantified rather than assumed. The project's own claimed value is therefore expressed as correct stress detection, warning lead time, uncertainty honesty, usability and irrigation-attention relevance. Prospective water-saving quantification is claimed only to the extent the commercial farmer-field irrigation-treatment arrangement actually supports it; where it does not, FIELDWISE reports detection, lead-time and uncertainty outcomes together with measured yield and quality. This disciplined framing is itself part of the importance of the contribution: it gives evaluators a defensible magnitude signal without overclaiming.

Technological and economic impact and its magnitude. The economic and technological contribution is anchored in a tangible research-to-application vehicle rather than a paper concept: the crop-configurable DrR web MVP with validated processing-tomato module (due month 24) provides a concrete route from validated research to external testing, while preserving the distinction between the fellow's pre-existing DrR background and the FIELDWISE foreground. Because the architecture is crop-configurable — reusable data-ingestion, uncertainty, visualisation and irrigation-attention components separated from crop-specific parameters — the same investment can support additional crop modules after crop-specific validation, multiplying the reach of a single fellowship's output. The magnitude of the economic contribution is deliberately not fabricated as an invented EUR/ha or fixed water-saving figure; instead the project measures the quantities from which later economic value can genuinely be assessed — irrigation water applied, water productivity, yield and marketable yield, quality indicators, intervention timing and warning lead time. The route to real-world uptake is made concrete by the AgroVIR operational/interoperability assessment (due month 30) and the Post-MSCA FMIS integration and exploitation roadmap (due month 30), which name the required interfaces, the exploitation route and the post-fellowship steps, with Krumatic supporting software implementation and Bulgarian farmer-facing uptake. This inter-sectoral chain is the mechanism by which FIELDWISE contributes to stimulated innovation, knowledge transfer and expanded career opportunities through the non-academic placement incentive (EI-05).

European and societal relevance and its scale. The societal magnitude is bounded and evidenced rather than rhetorical. Eurostat reports fresh vegetables cultivated over approximately 2.0 million hectares in the EU in 2023, and about 0.7 million EU farms cultivating fresh vegetables in the 2020 census — an indication of the scale of the horticultural domain in which scientifically transferable, plant-based irrigation decision support could ultimately matter, presented explicitly as a potential application domain and not as an immediate addressable market. Bulgaria supplies concrete downstream context for the project's cross-border replication logic: about 35.6 thousand hectares of main vegetable area and roughly 128 thousand tonnes of tomato in harvest 2024. The combination of Hungarian scientific and industrial environments, a real farmer validation setting, Bulgarian software and dissemination links through Krumatic, and a defined post-MSCA replication and re-validation route through MVCRI provides a realistic pathway toward wider reuse, contributing particularly to SDG 2, SDG 6, SDG 12 and SDG 13. This cross-border pathway also broadens public and practitioner engagement with the research (EI-03) through practitioner-oriented demonstrations and farmer-facing communication.

Importance, credibility and proportionality of the contribution. The importance of FIELDWISE's contribution rests on three features that keep magnitude claims credible. First, every quantified magnitude is either drawn from published literature and labelled as bounded context, or measured from the project's own prospective data — the proposal deliberately avoids inventing water-saving or economic figures. Second, the contribution is auditable: an eleven-KPI set (K1–K11) is defined so that each indicator measures something the project actually controls and delivers and each traces to a named deliverable, so the magnitude of delivery can be checked rather than asserted. Third, the design converts an apparent weakness — a single fellow on a single crop — into strength, because the transferable core, the crop-transfer gates and the post-MSCA MVCRI route extend the reach of the work beyond the 24-month scientific programme without over-committing the resources of one fellowship. Taken together, the scientific protocol and honest transfer result, the disciplined agricultural/environmental magnitude context, the concrete research-to-operation economic vehicle, and the evidenced European/Bulgarian scale give the evaluator a contribution whose magnitude is significant precisely because it is credible, controlled and reusable beyond the immediate case.

The methodological knowledge forms a basis for later crop-by-crop extension across irrigated high-value horticulture rather than an unsupported universalisation from processing tomato.

The model card, crop-transfer specification, prospective transferability report, two-way transfer and planned publications deliver increased and broadened R&I impact via enhanced networking/communication.

The model card, crop-transfer specification and transferability report plus the two-way transfer between the fellow and the ATK/ELTE/MATE environments deliver increased R&I capacity, output and knowledge transfer among European research organisations.

The development crop is processing tomato (roughly five seasons 2022-2026), the domain is irrigated high-value horticulture, and the project makes no fixed-percentage water-saving promise, reporting project-specific saving, yield, quality and uncertainty from prospective validation instead.
Comparable published studies demonstrate water-saving effects in the approximate 8-30% range under specific strategies, cited as bounded literature context and never as a project promise.

Named deliverables — Primary model, benchmark and model card; Spectral/UAV/Sentinel harmonisation and crop-transfer specification; Prospective transferability, uncertainty and limited-recalibration report (M18); Crop-configurable DrR web MVP with validated processing-tomato module (M24); AgroVIR operational/interoperability assessment (M30); Post-MSCA FMIS integration and exploitation roadmap (M30) — carry the impact contribution.
